decision.summary: Tenant reported a once-a-minute chirp from a 2019 sealed-battery CO alarm, now past its 7-year life. Treated as an urgent end-of-life replacement, not a confirmed CO emergency. Logged urgent and routine (fan) jobs, sent safety advice to tenant, and asked the landlord for approval.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue, or end-of-life alarm? How did you decide?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life alarm. A single chirp about once a minute is a fault/end-of-life signal, not a CO alarm sounding. The unit was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life, so it expired around April 2026, and it has a sealed battery so it cannot be a simple battery change. Not treated as an emergency, but CO was not ruled out, so safety advice was given and replacement is urgent.

answers.question: Who is responsible for fixing it, citing the tenancy clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 only makes the tenant replace batteries as required; the battery here is sealed, so the whole unit must be replaced, which is the landlord's job. Clause 12.9 means the tenant should test monthly and report faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) does not apply as the report was prompt and the alarm is past its life.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created urgent ticket JOB-101 and routine fan ticket JOB-102, requested landlord approval (APR-104), set a follow-up for 12 Oct, and texted Priya: don't remove the battery, leave and call 0800 111 999 (or 999) if the alarm sounds continuously or anyone feels unwell, replacement being arranged at no charge, target within 72 hours once approved, update by 12 Oct.

actions_claimed.description: SMS to tenant with safety advice and next steps

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't remove the battery or disable the alarm. Yours is a sealed unit fitted in 2019 and is likely at the end of its life, which causes a chirp, so we are arranging a replacement as an urgent job (target within 72 hours; we'll confirm once the landlord has approved). We can't rule out CO from a chirp alone, so if the alarm ever sounds continuously, or anyone has a headache, dizziness, nausea or feels drowsy, leave the flat, call the Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (999 if anyone is unwell) and don't use switches or flames. Your tenancy makes the landlord responsible for replacing a sealed alarm, so no charge to you. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan as a routine job. We'll update you by Monday 12 October.
